**Consequence:** the entire ingestion pipeline is plain HTTP + HTML parsing. No Playwright,
no browser pool, no per-page RAM budget. This removes the dominant infrastructure cost and
the most common source of flakiness in scraping projects.

### The JSON-LD payload (real sample, `halloween-the-game`)

```json
{
  "@type": "VideoGame",
  "name": "Halloween: The Game",
  "datePublished": "2026-09-08",
  "description": "It is Halloween night, 1978, ...",
  "image": "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/.../7-1776805800.jpg",
  "genre": "Survival",
  "gamePlatform": ["PlayStation 5", "Xbox Series X", "PC"],
  "publisher": [{"@type": "Organization", "name": "Gun Interactive"}],
  "trailer": {"@type": "VideoObject"},
  "aggregateRating": {"@type": "AggregateRating", "name": "Metascore"}
}
```

This one block covers **title, description, cover image, platforms, publisher, and trailer
link** — 6 of the 7 required fields, from a schema.org contract far more stable than CSS
classes. **Design rule: JSON-LD is the primary extractor; CSS selectors are the documented
fallback.** This is the main defence against Metacritic redesigns.

> **Note:** the field is `publisher`, **not** developer. The task asks for *Разработчик*
> (developer). These are genuinely different entities and JSON-LD gives us the publisher.
> See **OQ-3**.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### 1.1 Mandatory (from the brief)

| # | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FR-1 | Hourly job ingests **20 games not yet processed today** | "20" = per-run batch size |
| FR-2 | First run of a day → New Releases from `/game/` | Source A |
| FR-3 | Subsequent runs → `/browse/.../new/`, next page each time | Source B |
| FR-4 | Each new day the cycle restarts from Source A | Day = calendar day in fixed TZ (**OQ-1**) |
| FR-5 | Existing game is **updated**, not duplicated | Upsert on stable key |
| FR-6 | Capture title, cover, platform+Metascore+Userscore (N platforms), developer, description, video link | Platform data is 1..N per game |
| FR-7 | Separate LLM summaries for **critic** and **user** reviews (likes / dislikes) | Refreshable on re-crawl |
| FR-8 | Web UI: list, detail card, platform filter, title search, sort by rating | |
| FR-9 | Similar games from **our own DB**, clickable through to their card | |

### 1.2 Optional part 1 — YouTube let's-plays
Find let's-plays, take the **most popular**, transcribe the narration, derive a conclusion,
attach it to the game with a link to the video.

### 1.3 Optional part 2 — Realtime monitoring
Live worker status, processed counters, and a **force-run button**.

### 1.4 Deliverables
Repository link, a **live running service**, and full raw JSONL AI transcripts. The "live
service" requirement makes deployability a first-class constraint, not an afterthought — it
is weighted in every technology choice below.

### 1.5 Derived requirements (implied — flagged, not silently invented)

- **DR-1** Per-platform scores imply a `game_platform` child table, not columns on `game`.
- **DR-2** "Not processed today" implies a persisted per-day ledger surviving restarts.
- **DR-3** "Next page each run" implies a persisted per-day cursor.
- **DR-4** Summaries "may be updated" implies storing a content fingerprint to avoid paying
  an LLM call when reviews have not changed.
- **DR-5** The service must show useful data within minutes of a cold deploy, or a reviewer
  opening the link sees an empty list. Drives seed-on-first-boot (**OQ-9**).

---

## 2. Non-functional requirements

| Area | Target | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | Best-effort single node; survives restart with zero data loss | Demo service, not a bank |
| Politeness | ≤ 1 req/s to Metacritic, 1 concurrent connection, backoff on 429/5xx | Avoids IP ban that would kill the demo |
| Batch latency | 20 games ≤ 10 min wall clock | Must finish well inside the 1 h window |
| UI latency | list p95 < 300 ms, detail p95 < 400 ms | Indexed queries, no N+1 |
| Durability | All progress in Postgres; process is stateless | Restart-safety requirement |
| Cost | ≤ ~$5–10 for the evaluation period | See §18 |
| Observability | Every run auditable after the fact | Required to *prove* correctness to the reviewer |
| Reproducibility | `docker compose up` → working service | Evaluator convenience |

---

## 3. User flows

**U1 — Evaluator opens the service.** Lands on list, sees populated data immediately
(seeded), can search/filter/sort without reading docs.

**U2 — Browse & filter.** Filter by platform, search by title (debounced), sort by
Metascore/Userscore/date. Filters live in URL query params → shareable, back-button correct.

**U3 — Game card.** Cover, description, developer, per-platform score table, trailer embed,
critic summary, user summary, YouTube conclusion, similar games.

**U4 — Similar-game traversal.** Click a similar game → its card. Enables the "browse
around" behaviour an evaluator uses to judge data quality.

**U5 — Monitoring.** Live dashboard: run state, worker states, counters, per-item progress,
errors, day-cursor position.

**U6 — Force run.** Click → immediate run. Must be safe when a run is already in flight: UI
disables the button and reports "already running" rather than double-processing.

**U7 — Cold-start recovery (operator).** After a crash the service resumes without manual
intervention and the dashboard explains what happened.

---

## 4. Backend components

Single deployable Node.js/TypeScript app (**OQ-2**) with internal module boundaries:

- **HTTP API** — REST for the UI (`/api/games`, `/api/games/:slug`, `/api/platforms`,
  `/api/runs`, `/api/status`, `POST /api/runs`).
- **Realtime gateway** — SSE stream of run/worker events (§11).
- **Scheduler** — in-process cron with DB lock (§7).
- **Orchestrator** — decides *what* the batch is (day-plan logic, CORE section).
- **Fetcher** — polite HTTP client: UA, rate limit, retry, conditional GET, caching.
- **Parsers** — `listParser` (both sources), `gameParser` (JSON-LD first), `reviewParser`.
- **Enrichment services** — LLM summarizer, similarity, YouTube.
- **Repositories** — all SQL; the only layer touching the DB.
- **AI transcript logger** — appends every LLM/API exchange to JSONL (deliverable §1.4).

Rationale for a modular monolith over microservices: the workload is tiny, the deliverable
must be trivially runnable, and distributed tracing across services would cost more than it
teaches here. Boundaries stay clean so extraction remains possible.

---

## 5. Frontend components

- `GameList` — card grid, pagination/infinite scroll, skeletons.
- `FilterBar` — platform multi-select, debounced search, sort dropdown; state in URL.
- `GameCard` (detail) — hero, `PlatformScoreTable`, `TrailerEmbed`, `ReviewSummary` ×2
  (visually distinct critic vs user), `YouTubeConclusion`, `SimilarGames`.
- `MonitoringDashboard` — `RunStatusPanel`, `WorkerGrid`, `CounterTiles`, `EventLog`,
  `ForceRunButton`, `DayPlanIndicator` (shows Source A/B and page cursor).
- Empty/error/loading states throughout — an evaluator *will* hit them.

**[ASSUMPTION]** SSR framework (Next.js) for fast first paint and simple deployment; the UI
is read-mostly so this is low-risk. See **OQ-2**.

---

## 6. Background workers

Pipeline stages per game, each independently retryable and independently persisted:

1. **discover** — resolve the batch (list pages → slugs).
2. **fetchGame** — detail page → JSON-LD → core fields + platforms.
3. **fetchReviews** — critic + user review pages.
4. **summarize** — 2 LLM calls (skipped if review fingerprint unchanged — DR-4).
5. **similar** — compute neighbours.
6. **youtube** — search → pick top → transcript → conclusion.

**Key design decision — staged persistence.** Each stage commits its own result as it
completes, and each game carries a per-stage status. A crash after stage 2 does **not**
discard stages 1–2 on retry; the item resumes at stage 3. This is what makes "partially
completed processing" safe (§14).

**Failure isolation:** stages 4–6 are *enrichment*. Their failure must never prevent the
game being saved and displayed — the game is `complete_core` with `summary_status=failed`.
Only stages 1–3 can fail an item outright.

Concurrency: a small worker pool (default 4) over *items*, but the Metacritic fetcher is
globally rate-limited so politeness holds regardless of pool size (§15).

---

## 7. Scheduler

Hourly trigger. Every run — scheduled or forced — goes through **one** code path:
`startRun(trigger: 'cron' | 'manual')`.

**[ASSUMPTION]** In-process scheduler (`node-cron`) + Postgres advisory lock, rather than an
external scheduler. Justification: single-node deployment, and the lock is required anyway
for the force-run button. Migration path to a real queue noted in **OQ-2**.

Correctness rules:
- Acquire `pg_try_advisory_lock` before starting; if not acquired, exit as `skipped`.
- Lock is session-scoped → **released automatically by Postgres if the process dies**. This
  is the primary defence against a crashed run wedging the scheduler forever.
- Missed ticks (process down) are **not** back-filled; the next tick just runs. The day-plan
  makes catch-up naturally correct because it derives from DB state, not tick counting.

---

## 8. Database

**PostgreSQL** — chosen for transactional upserts, `ON CONFLICT`, advisory locks, `pg_trgm`
fuzzy title search, and JSONB. All of these are actually used here. SQLite would fail the
concurrency and search requirements.

### Core schema (abridged)

```
game
  id, slug UNIQUE, title, description, cover_url, trailer_url,
  developer, publisher, genres[], release_date,
  metascore_overall, userscore_overall,     -- denormalised for sorting
  content_hash, first_seen_at, last_updated_at

game_platform            -- DR-1: 1..N per game
  game_id, platform_slug, platform_name, metascore, userscore,
  critic_count, user_count
  PRIMARY KEY (game_id, platform_slug)

review_snapshot
  game_id, kind ENUM('critic','user'), raw_reviews JSONB,
  reviews_fingerprint, fetched_at

review_summary
  game_id, kind, likes TEXT, dislikes TEXT, verdict TEXT,
  source_fingerprint, model, token_usage, generated_at
  UNIQUE (game_id, kind)

youtube_insight
  game_id, video_id, video_url, title, channel, view_count,
  transcript_source, conclusion, generated_at

similar_game
  game_id, similar_game_id, score, method, computed_at
  PRIMARY KEY (game_id, similar_game_id)

-- Scheduling / idempotency core
processing_day           -- one row per calendar day
  day DATE PRIMARY KEY, phase ENUM('new_releases','browse','exhausted'),
  browse_page INT, new_releases_done BOOL

daily_processed_game     -- THE "not processed today" ledger (DR-2)
  day DATE, game_slug TEXT, run_id, status, stages JSONB, updated_at
  PRIMARY KEY (day, game_slug)

run
  id, trigger, status, started_at, finished_at,
  planned_count, processed_count, failed_count, skipped_count, error

run_event                -- append-only audit + realtime feed
  id, run_id, ts, level, stage, game_slug, message, payload JSONB
```

`daily_processed_game` with PK `(day, game_slug)` is the linchpin: simultaneously the
ledger, the idempotency guard, and the concurrency guard (§14, §15).

Indexes: `game(metascore_overall DESC)`, `game(release_date DESC)`,
`game USING gin(title gin_trgm_ops)`, `game_platform(platform_slug)`,
`run_event(run_id, ts DESC)`.

---

## 9. External integrations

| Service | Use | Auth | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metacritic | Listings, detail, reviews | none | Layout change / IP block — **High** |
| LLM provider | Summaries, conclusion | API key | Cost, latency — Low |
| YouTube Data API v3 | Let's-play search | API key | 10 000 u/day quota; search = 100 u → ~100 searches/day — **Medium** |
| Transcript source | Narration → text | varies | **Highest technical risk** — see deep dive |
| Image CDN | Covers | none | Hotlink/referrer policy — Low |

---

## 10. LLM / AI components

**Three distinct jobs**, deliberately separated:

1. **Critic summary** — input: critic reviews. Output: `likes`, `dislikes`, `verdict`.
2. **User summary** — input: user reviews. Same shape, different voice/prompt.
3. **YouTube conclusion** — input: transcript. Output: a short conclusion.

Design rules:
- **Structured output** (JSON schema / tool-use) — never free-text parsing.
- **Input budget:** cap at N reviews and M chars each, sampled across the score range (not
  just the top) so the summary reflects the real spread of opinion. Truncation is recorded
  so the summary is honest about its basis.
- **Fingerprint gate (DR-4):** hash the review set; skip the call if unchanged. Single
  biggest cost lever — steady-state re-crawls become nearly free.
- **Grounding:** prompt forbids inventing facts absent from the supplied reviews.
- **Zero-review case:** do **not** call the LLM; store an explicit "not enough reviews"
  state. Many brand-new indie games on the "new" listing have no reviews at all — this is
  the common case, not an edge case.
- **Full JSONL transcript logging** of every request/response — a required deliverable.

**Model choice [ASSUMPTION]:** a small/cheap model (Haiku-class) suffices for summarising
supplied text; this is not a reasoning-heavy task. See **OQ-6**.

---

## 11. Monitoring (optional part 2)

- **Transport [ASSUMPTION]:** **SSE**, not WebSockets. Data flows server→client only; SSE
  auto-reconnects, traverses proxies cleanly, and is far less code. See **OQ-7**.
- **Event bus:** stages emit events → persisted to `run_event` → broadcast to subscribers.
  Persisting *before* broadcasting means a client connecting mid-run can replay recent
  history rather than see an empty screen.
- **Dashboard:** current run + trigger, per-worker state (idle/fetching/summarising +
  current slug), counters, today's plan (phase, page cursor, processed-today count), rolling
  event log, last error.
- **Force-run button** → `POST /api/runs`; returns `202` with run id, or `409` if a run holds
  the lock. UI reflects both outcomes distinctly.
- Plus `/healthz` and `/readyz` for the host platform.

---

## 12. Error handling

Explicit taxonomy, because the correct reaction differs per class:

| Class | Example | Reaction |
|---|---|---|
| Transient network | timeout, ECONNRESET, 5xx | Retry w/ backoff |
| Rate limit | 429 | Retry, honour `Retry-After`, slow global limiter |
| Blocked | 403 challenge | **Abort run**, mark `blocked` — retrying makes it worse |
| Parse failure | JSON-LD absent & selectors miss | Fail item, save raw HTML sample, continue run |
| Partial data | no reviews / no trailer | **Not an error** — nullable field |
| LLM failure | timeout, refusal, bad JSON | Retry once, then mark summary failed; game still saved |
| Quota exhausted | YouTube 403 quota | Disable that stage for the day, continue |
| DB error | constraint violation | Fail item, log, continue |

**Guiding principle: one bad game must never fail the batch.** Item errors are caught at
item scope; only infrastructure errors (DB down, blocked) abort a run.

---

## 13. Retry strategy

- HTTP: 3 attempts, exponential backoff + jitter (1 s → 2 s → 4 s), retry only idempotent
  GETs and only transient/429 classes.
- LLM: 2 attempts; malformed structured output counts as retryable once.
- Item-level: a failed item is **not** retried inside the same run (avoids head-of-line
  blocking). It stays unmarked in the day-ledger and is naturally re-attempted by the next
  hourly run — the schedule itself is the retry mechanism.
- Circuit breaker: N consecutive Metacritic failures → abort run early, record reason.
  Prevents burning an hour hammering a site that is blocking us.

---

## 14. Idempotency & crash-safety

This is the heart of the brief, so it is specified precisely.

**Two-phase claim/complete against `daily_processed_game`:**

1. **Claim:** `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (day, game_slug) DO NOTHING RETURNING *`.
   Row returned → this worker owns the item. Nothing returned → someone else owns it, skip.
   The claim is atomic, so it doubles as the concurrency guard.
2. **Process** stages, persisting each stage's output as it completes.
3. **Complete:** update the row to `done` with stage detail.

**Recovery from every failure mode in the brief:**

| Scenario | Guarantee | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **App restart** | No duplicates, no loss | All state in Postgres; advisory lock auto-released on disconnect; next tick recomputes the plan from DB |
| **Worker crash** | Item retried, others unaffected | Item left `claimed`; a **stale-claim reaper** (claimed older than lease T) resets it to pending |
| **Job re-run** | Safe | Ledger claim rejects already-done slugs; `ON CONFLICT` upserts make game writes idempotent |
| **Parallel workers** | No double-processing | Atomic claim (row-level); only one wins each slug |
| **Partial processing** | Resumes, does not restart | Per-stage status + stage-level persistence; completed stages skipped on retry |

**Upsert key [ASSUMPTION]:** the Metacritic **slug** — stable, unique, present in every URL.
Titles are not unique (remakes/re-releases). See **OQ-4**.

The **stale-claim lease** is the subtle one: without it, a worker that dies mid-item leaves
that slug claimed forever and it silently never gets processed that day. The reaper closes
this hole.

---

## 15. Concurrency

Three independent levels, deliberately decoupled:

- **Run level:** at most one run globally — Postgres advisory lock. Protects against
  cron + force-run collision and against two app instances.
- **Item level:** worker pool (default 4) pulling claimed items. Safe because claiming is
  atomic.
- **Network level:** a **global token-bucket limiter shared by all workers**, ≤ 1 req/s to
  Metacritic. Critically, politeness is decoupled from pool size — raising concurrency never
  raises request rate against Metacritic. LLM/YouTube have separate limits.

Ordering: the brief implies sequential source order (A then B). The *plan* is ordered;
execution within a batch may be parallel — preserving required semantics without serialising
I/O.

---

## 16. Security

- Secrets via environment only; never committed. `.env.example` documents required keys.
- **Force-run endpoint must be protected** — it is an unauthenticated compute/cost trigger on
  a public URL. Recommend a shared-secret header or basic auth on write endpoints. **OQ-8**.
- Rate-limit write endpoints; strict input validation (zod) on all query params.
- SQL injection: parameterised queries only.
- XSS: scraped and LLM text is untrusted → escape on render; never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  Sanitise/allowlist embedded video URLs (known YouTube/Metacritic hosts only).
- SSRF: only fetch allowlisted hosts.
- No PII stored; user reviews are public content. Respect robots.txt and identify the bot
  honestly in the UA.

---

## 17. Performance

- Batch: 20 games × ~3 requests ≈ 60 requests at 1 req/s ≈ 1–2 min network-bound, plus LLM
  time (parallel, capped) → comfortably inside 10 min.
- Conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified) on re-crawled pages saves bandwidth and time.
- UI: server-side pagination, indexed sorts, trigram index for search, aggregates
  denormalised onto `game` to avoid per-row joins in the list view.
- Images: hotlink Metacritic CDN with lazy loading (**OQ-10** covers the alternative).
- Similarity computed on write, cached in `similar_game` — never computed per page view.

---

## 18. Cost

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| LLM summaries | 2 calls/game; cheap model; fingerprint gate makes re-crawls ~free → **low single-digit $** |
| YouTube API | Free tier; ~100 searches/day ceiling is the real constraint |
| Transcripts | Free if captions used; **paid ASR is the cost risk** (**OQ-5**) |
| Hosting | Small VPS / free-tier PaaS + managed Postgres ≈ **$0–7/mo** |
| **Total** | **≈ $5–10 for the evaluation period** |

Main cost lever is the fingerprint gate; second is ASR avoidance.

---

## CORE: Game processing logic (the central requirement)

### Day plan

`processing_day` holds, per calendar day: `phase`, `browse_page`, `new_releases_done`.

```
resolveBatch(day, N=20):
  ensure processing_day row for `day` (INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)

  if phase == 'new_releases':
      candidates = first 20 slugs from /game/   (New Releases)
      claimed    = claim(candidates)            -- skips already-done-today
      if claimed < N: top up from browse pages (advance cursor)
      when the New Releases set is fully processed today -> phase = 'browse'

  if phase == 'browse':
      loop:
        page        = browse_page
        candidates  = slugs from /browse/.../new/?page=page
        claimed    += claim(candidates)
        browse_page = page + 1                  -- persisted immediately
        until claimed == N or page limit hit
```

Because the batch derives from **DB state**, not run counters, it is automatically correct
after restarts, missed ticks, and manual runs.

### Daily reset

New calendar day → no `processing_day` row → created with `phase='new_releases'`,
`browse_page=1`. The cycle restarts naturally. **[ASSUMPTION]** the boundary is a fixed
configured timezone (not server-local) so behaviour is deterministic — **OQ-1**.

### VERIFIED RISK — the "next page" cursor is not stable

Live probing found that **page 1 and page 2 of the browse listing share 17 of 33 links**
**[VERIFIED]**. The listing is sorted by release date descending *including future-dated
releases* — page 1 was full of `Sep 7, 2026` and even `Sep 8, 2026` entries. New games are
inserted at the top continuously, so rows shift rightward as we paginate.

Naive "page N per run" logic therefore **re-reads games already handled and silently skips
others**. This would have been a real correctness bug found only in production.

**Mitigation (recommended):** treat the page cursor as a *hint*, not a source of truth. The
ledger (`daily_processed_game`) is authoritative — already-claimed slugs are filtered out and
the fetcher keeps advancing pages until it has collected N genuinely-new slugs. Overlap
becomes harmless; skipping is prevented. This is why "top up until N claimed" is a loop, not
a single page read.

### Update vs insert

`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE` on `game`; child rows (`game_platform`) reconciled
per run. `first_seen_at` preserved, `last_updated_at` bumped. Enrichment tables keyed to
allow refresh (FR-7).

---

## Deep dives

### Scraping Metacritic
Two list shapes + detail + 2 review pages. **JSON-LD first, CSS fallback**, with a parser
version recorded per game so stale extractions are identifiable after a site change. Persist
a raw HTML sample on parse failure for offline debugging. Golden-file parser tests (committed
HTML fixtures) so a Metacritic redesign is caught by CI rather than by silent data loss.
Honest UA identifying the bot.

### Reviews
Both endpoints are server-rendered **[VERIFIED]** — 10 critic blocks with scores and full
quote text were extracted from `elden-ring/critic-reviews/` over plain HTTP. Capture score,
outlet/author, date, text. **Zero reviews is the normal case for brand-new indie games** —
the pipeline must treat it as valid, not as failure. Review pagination capped at the first
page(s) (**OQ-11**).

### LLM summarization
See §10. Structured output, input sampled across the score spectrum, fingerprint-gated,
grounded prompt, JSONL-logged.

### Similar games
**[ASSUMPTION]** Start with cheap, explainable content similarity: shared genres + platform
overlap + developer/publisher match + title trigram, weighted. Deterministic, zero marginal
cost, no embedding infrastructure, easy to justify in review. Embeddings are the upgrade path
(**OQ-12**). Must exclude self, require a minimum score (better to show 2 good matches than 6
poor ones), and recompute as the corpus grows — early games have few candidates because the
DB is small.

### YouTube integration
Search `"<title> let's play|gameplay"` → rank by view count → transcript → conclusion.
**The transcript step is the highest technical risk in the optional scope:** many gaming
videos have no human captions, auto-captions are often unavailable through official APIs, and
third-party scrapers are fragile and ToS-grey, while ASR costs money and time.
Recommendation: attempt captions; if unavailable, **degrade gracefully** to a
metadata/description-based conclusion clearly labelled as such, rather than failing.
See **OQ-5**.

### Realtime monitoring
See §11. SSE, persist-then-broadcast, replayable recent history.

---

## Recommended MVP scope

| Phase | Content |
|---|---|
| **0 — skeleton** | Repo, Docker Compose, migrations, health checks, CI |
| **1 — mandatory core** | Fetcher, parsers, day plan + ledger, upserts, hourly cron |
| **2 — mandatory UI** | List, detail, filter, search, sort |
| **3 — AI** | Review summaries (critic + user), JSONL logging |
| **4 — similar games** | Content-based |
| **5 — optional 2** | Monitoring + force run *(cheap, highly visible)* |
| **6 — optional 1** | YouTube *(most expensive, riskiest — behind a flag)* |

Phases 1–4 satisfy the mandatory brief completely. Phase 5 is deliberately sequenced before
Phase 6 because it is lower-risk, lower-cost, and far more visible to an evaluator per hour
invested.

# Technical Discovery — Metacritic Games Service

**Status:** draft for Product/Tech Lead review
**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Author:** Lead Software Engineer / Solution Architect

> Statements marked **[VERIFIED]** were confirmed by live probing of Metacritic on
> 2026-09-07 (raw HTTP, no browser). Statements marked **[ASSUMPTION]** are design
> decisions needing your sign-off. Open items are tracked in `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.

---

## 0. Ground truth established during discovery

Before designing anything I probed the real endpoints, because the biggest cost driver in
this project is *"do we need a headless browser or not"*. The answer is **no**, and that
changes the whole architecture.

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /game/` (plain curl + normal UA) | **200**, 969 KB, ~1.1 s — no JS challenge **[VERIFIED]** |
| `GET /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/` | **200**, 342 KB, ~0.7 s **[VERIFIED]** |
| `__NEXT_DATA__` blob present | **No** — content is server-rendered HTML **[VERIFIED]** |
| JSON-LD on detail page | **Yes**: `VideoGame`, `AggregateRating`, `VideoObject`, `ImageObject`, `Organization` **[VERIFIED]** |
| Critic reviews `/game/<slug>/critic-reviews/` | **200**, review text + per-critic scores in raw HTML **[VERIFIED]** |
| User reviews `/game/<slug>/user-reviews/` | **200**, same shape **[VERIFIED]** |
| `robots.txt` | Blocks named bots (GPTBot, CCBot, AhrefsBot...). **No `Disallow` on `/browse/` or `/game/`** for a generic UA. Publishes `games.xml` sitemap **[VERIFIED]** |

**Consequence:** the entire ingestion pipeline is plain HTTP + HTML parsing. No Playwright,
no browser pool, no per-page RAM budget. This removes the dominant infrastructure cost and
the most common source of flakiness in scraping projects.

### The JSON-LD payload (real sample, `halloween-the-game`)

```json
{
  "@type": "VideoGame",
  "name": "Halloween: The Game",
  "datePublished": "2026-09-08",
  "description": "It is Halloween night, 1978, ...",
  "image": "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/.../7-1776805800.jpg",
  "genre": "Survival",
  "gamePlatform": ["PlayStation 5", "Xbox Series X", "PC"],
  "publisher": [{"@type": "Organization", "name": "Gun Interactive"}],
  "trailer": {"@type": "VideoObject"},
  "aggregateRating": {"@type": "AggregateRating", "name": "Metascore"}
}
```

This one block covers **title, description, cover image, platforms, publisher, and trailer
link** — 6 of the 7 required fields, from a schema.org contract far more stable than CSS
classes. **Design rule: JSON-LD is the primary extractor; CSS selectors are the documented
fallback.** This is the main defence against Metacritic redesigns.

> **Note:** the field is `publisher`, **not** developer. The task asks for *Разработчик*
> (developer). These are genuinely different entities and JSON-LD gives us the publisher.
> See **OQ-3**.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### 1.1 Mandatory (from the brief)

| # | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FR-1 | Hourly job ingests **20 games not yet processed today** | "20" = per-run batch size |
| FR-2 | First run of a day → New Releases from `/game/` | Source A |
| FR-3 | Subsequent runs → `/browse/.../new/`, next page each time | Source B |
| FR-4 | Each new day the cycle restarts from Source A | Day = calendar day in fixed TZ (**OQ-1**) |
| FR-5 | Existing game is **updated**, not duplicated | Upsert on stable key |
| FR-6 | Capture title, cover, platform+Metascore+Userscore (N platforms), developer, description, video link | Platform data is 1..N per game |
| FR-7 | Separate LLM summaries for **critic** and **user** reviews (likes / dislikes) | Refreshable on re-crawl |
| FR-8 | Web UI: list, detail card, platform filter, title search, sort by rating | |
| FR-9 | Similar games from **our own DB**, clickable through to their card | |

### 1.2 Optional part 1 — YouTube let's-plays
Find let's-plays, take the **most popular**, transcribe the narration, derive a conclusion,
attach it to the game with a link to the video.

### 1.3 Optional part 2 — Realtime monitoring
Live worker status, processed counters, and a **force-run button**.

### 1.4 Deliverables
Repository link, a **live running service**, and full raw JSONL AI transcripts. The "live
service" requirement makes deployability a first-class constraint, not an afterthought — it
is weighted in every technology choice below.

### 1.5 Derived requirements (implied — flagged, not silently invented)

- **DR-1** Per-platform scores imply a `game_platform` child table, not columns on `game`.
- **DR-2** "Not processed today" implies a persisted per-day ledger surviving restarts.
- **DR-3** "Next page each run" implies a persisted per-day cursor.
- **DR-4** Summaries "may be updated" implies storing a content fingerprint to avoid paying
  an LLM call when reviews have not changed.
- **DR-5** The service must show useful data within minutes of a cold deploy, or a reviewer
  opening the link sees an empty list. Drives seed-on-first-boot (**OQ-9**).

---

## 2. Non-functional requirements

| Area | Target | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | Best-effort single node; survives restart with zero data loss | Demo service, not a bank |
| Politeness | ≤ 1 req/s to Metacritic, 1 concurrent connection, backoff on 429/5xx | Avoids IP ban that would kill the demo |
| Batch latency | 20 games ≤ 10 min wall clock | Must finish well inside the 1 h window |
| UI latency | list p95 < 300 ms, detail p95 < 400 ms | Indexed queries, no N+1 |
| Durability | All progress in Postgres; process is stateless | Restart-safety requirement |
| Cost | ≤ ~$5–10 for the evaluation period | See §18 |
| Observability | Every run auditable after the fact | Required to *prove* correctness to the reviewer |
| Reproducibility | `docker compose up` → working service | Evaluator convenience |

---

## 3. User flows

**U1 — Evaluator opens the service.** Lands on list, sees populated data immediately
(seeded), can search/filter/sort without reading docs.

**U2 — Browse & filter.** Filter by platform, search by title (debounced), sort by
Metascore/Userscore/date. Filters live in URL query params → shareable, back-button correct.

**U3 — Game card.** Cover, description, developer, per-platform score table, trailer embed,
critic summary, user summary, YouTube conclusion, similar games.

**U4 — Similar-game traversal.** Click a similar game → its card. Enables the "browse
around" behaviour an evaluator uses to judge data quality.

**U5 — Monitoring.** Live dashboard: run state, worker states, counters, per-item progress,
errors, day-cursor position.

**U6 — Force run.** Click → immediate run. Must be safe when a run is already in flight: UI
disables the button and reports "already running" rather than double-processing.

**U7 — Cold-start recovery (operator).** After a crash the service resumes without manual
intervention and the dashboard explains what happened.

---

## 4. Backend components

Single deployable Node.js/TypeScript app (**OQ-2**) with internal module boundaries:

- **HTTP API** — REST for the UI (`/api/games`, `/api/games/:slug`, `/api/platforms`,
  `/api/runs`, `/api/status`, `POST /api/runs`).
- **Realtime gateway** — SSE stream of run/worker events (§11).
- **Scheduler** — in-process cron with DB lock (§7).
- **Orchestrator** — decides *what* the batch is (day-plan logic, CORE section).
- **Fetcher** — polite HTTP client: UA, rate limit, retry, conditional GET, caching.
- **Parsers** — `listParser` (both sources), `gameParser` (JSON-LD first), `reviewParser`.
- **Enrichment services** — LLM summarizer, similarity, YouTube.
- **Repositories** — all SQL; the only layer touching the DB.
- **AI transcript logger** — appends every LLM/API exchange to JSONL (deliverable §1.4).

Rationale for a modular monolith over microservices: the workload is tiny, the deliverable
must be trivially runnable, and distributed tracing across services would cost more than it
teaches here. Boundaries stay clean so extraction remains possible.

---

## 5. Frontend components

- `GameList` — card grid, pagination/infinite scroll, skeletons.
- `FilterBar` — platform multi-select, debounced search, sort dropdown; state in URL.
- `GameCard` (detail) — hero, `PlatformScoreTable`, `TrailerEmbed`, `ReviewSummary` ×2
  (visually distinct critic vs user), `YouTubeConclusion`, `SimilarGames`.
- `MonitoringDashboard` — `RunStatusPanel`, `WorkerGrid`, `CounterTiles`, `EventLog`,
  `ForceRunButton`, `DayPlanIndicator` (shows Source A/B and page cursor).
- Empty/error/loading states throughout — an evaluator *will* hit them.

**[ASSUMPTION]** SSR framework (Next.js) for fast first paint and simple deployment; the UI
is read-mostly so this is low-risk. See **OQ-2**.

---

## 6. Background workers

Pipeline stages per game, each independently retryable and independently persisted:

1. **discover** — resolve the batch (list pages → slugs).
2. **fetchGame** — detail page → JSON-LD → core fields + platforms.
3. **fetchReviews** — critic + user review pages.
4. **summarize** — 2 LLM calls (skipped if review fingerprint unchanged — DR-4).
5. **similar** — compute neighbours.
6. **youtube** — search → pick top → transcript → conclusion.

**Key design decision — staged persistence.** Each stage commits its own result as it
completes, and each game carries a per-stage status. A crash after stage 2 does **not**
discard stages 1–2 on retry; the item resumes at stage 3. This is what makes "partially
completed processing" safe (§14).

**Failure isolation:** stages 4–6 are *enrichment*. Their failure must never prevent the
game being saved and displayed — the game is `complete_core` with `summary_status=failed`.
Only stages 1–3 can fail an item outright.

Concurrency: a small worker pool (default 4) over *items*, but the Metacritic fetcher is
globally rate-limited so politeness holds regardless of pool size (§15).

---

## 7. Scheduler

Hourly trigger. Every run — scheduled or forced — goes through **one** code path:
`startRun(trigger: 'cron' | 'manual')`.

**[ASSUMPTION]** In-process scheduler (`node-cron`) + Postgres advisory lock, rather than an
external scheduler. Justification: single-node deployment, and the lock is required anyway
for the force-run button. Migration path to a real queue noted in **OQ-2**.

Correctness rules:
- Acquire `pg_try_advisory_lock` before starting; if not acquired, exit as `skipped`.
- Lock is session-scoped → **released automatically by Postgres if the process dies**. This
  is the primary defence against a crashed run wedging the scheduler forever.
- Missed ticks (process down) are **not** back-filled; the next tick just runs. The day-plan
  makes catch-up naturally correct because it derives from DB state, not tick counting.

---

## 8. Database

**PostgreSQL** — chosen for transactional upserts, `ON CONFLICT`, advisory locks, `pg_trgm`
fuzzy title search, and JSONB. All of these are actually used here. SQLite would fail the
concurrency and search requirements.

### Core schema (abridged)

```
game
  id, slug UNIQUE, title, description, cover_url, trailer_url,
  developer, publisher, genres[], release_date,
  metascore_overall, userscore_overall,     -- denormalised for sorting
  content_hash, first_seen_at, last_updated_at

game_platform            -- DR-1: 1..N per game
  game_id, platform_slug, platform_name, metascore, userscore,
  critic_count, user_count
  PRIMARY KEY (game_id, platform_slug)

review_snapshot
  game_id, kind ENUM('critic','user'), raw_reviews JSONB,
  reviews_fingerprint, fetched_at

review_summary
  game_id, kind, likes TEXT, dislikes TEXT, verdict TEXT,
  source_fingerprint, model, token_usage, generated_at
  UNIQUE (game_id, kind)

youtube_insight
  game_id, video_id, video_url, title, channel, view_count,
  transcript_source, conclusion, generated_at

similar_game
  game_id, similar_game_id, score, method, computed_at
  PRIMARY KEY (game_id, similar_game_id)

-- Scheduling / idempotency core
processing_day           -- one row per calendar day
  day DATE PRIMARY KEY, phase ENUM('new_releases','browse','exhausted'),
  browse_page INT, new_releases_done BOOL

daily_processed_game     -- THE "not processed today" ledger (DR-2)
  day DATE, game_slug TEXT, run_id, status, stages JSONB, updated_at
  PRIMARY KEY (day, game_slug)

run
  id, trigger, status, started_at, finished_at,
  planned_count, processed_count, failed_count, skipped_count, error

run_event                -- append-only audit + realtime feed
  id, run_id, ts, level, stage, game_slug, message, payload JSONB
```

`daily_processed_game` with PK `(day, game_slug)` is the linchpin: simultaneously the
ledger, the idempotency guard, and the concurrency guard (§14, §15).

Indexes: `game(metascore_overall DESC)`, `game(release_date DESC)`,
`game USING gin(title gin_trgm_ops)`, `game_platform(platform_slug)`,
`run_event(run_id, ts DESC)`.

---

## 9. External integrations

| Service | Use | Auth | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metacritic | Listings, detail, reviews | none | Layout change / IP block — **High** |
| LLM provider | Summaries, conclusion | API key | Cost, latency — Low |
| YouTube Data API v3 | Let's-play search | API key | 10 000 u/day quota; search = 100 u → ~100 searches/day — **Medium** |
| Transcript source | Narration → text | varies | **Highest technical risk** — see deep dive |
| Image CDN | Covers | none | Hotlink/referrer policy — Low |

---

## 10. LLM / AI components

**Three distinct jobs**, deliberately separated:

1. **Critic summary** — input: critic reviews. Output: `likes`, `dislikes`, `verdict`.
2. **User summary** — input: user reviews. Same shape, different voice/prompt.
3. **YouTube conclusion** — input: transcript. Output: a short conclusion.

Design rules:
- **Structured output** (JSON schema / tool-use) — never free-text parsing.
- **Input budget:** cap at N reviews and M chars each, sampled across the score range (not
  just the top) so the summary reflects the real spread of opinion. Truncation is recorded
  so the summary is honest about its basis.
- **Fingerprint gate (DR-4):** hash the review set; skip the call if unchanged. Single
  biggest cost lever — steady-state re-crawls become nearly free.
- **Grounding:** prompt forbids inventing facts absent from the supplied reviews.
- **Zero-review case:** do **not** call the LLM; store an explicit "not enough reviews"
  state. Many brand-new indie games on the "new" listing have no reviews at all — this is
  the common case, not an edge case.
- **Full JSONL transcript logging** of every request/response — a required deliverable.

**Model choice [ASSUMPTION]:** a small/cheap model (Haiku-class) suffices for summarising
supplied text; this is not a reasoning-heavy task. See **OQ-6**.

---

## 11. Monitoring (optional part 2)

- **Transport [ASSUMPTION]:** **SSE**, not WebSockets. Data flows server→client only; SSE
  auto-reconnects, traverses proxies cleanly, and is far less code. See **OQ-7**.
- **Event bus:** stages emit events → persisted to `run_event` → broadcast to subscribers.
  Persisting *before* broadcasting means a client connecting mid-run can replay recent
  history rather than see an empty screen.
- **Dashboard:** current run + trigger, per-worker state (idle/fetching/summarising +
  current slug), counters, today's plan (phase, page cursor, processed-today count), rolling
  event log, last error.
- **Force-run button** → `POST /api/runs`; returns `202` with run id, or `409` if a run holds
  the lock. UI reflects both outcomes distinctly.
- Plus `/healthz` and `/readyz` for the host platform.

---

## 12. Error handling

Explicit taxonomy, because the correct reaction differs per class:

| Class | Example | Reaction |
|---|---|---|
| Transient network | timeout, ECONNRESET, 5xx | Retry w/ backoff |
| Rate limit | 429 | Retry, honour `Retry-After`, slow global limiter |
| Blocked | 403 challenge | **Abort run**, mark `blocked` — retrying makes it worse |
| Parse failure | JSON-LD absent & selectors miss | Fail item, save raw HTML sample, continue run |
| Partial data | no reviews / no trailer | **Not an error** — nullable field |
| LLM failure | timeout, refusal, bad JSON | Retry once, then mark summary failed; game still saved |
| Quota exhausted | YouTube 403 quota | Disable that stage for the day, continue |
| DB error | constraint violation | Fail item, log, continue |

**Guiding principle: one bad game must never fail the batch.** Item errors are caught at
item scope; only infrastructure errors (DB down, blocked) abort a run.

---

## 13. Retry strategy

- HTTP: 3 attempts, exponential backoff + jitter (1 s → 2 s → 4 s), retry only idempotent
  GETs and only transient/429 classes.
- LLM: 2 attempts; malformed structured output counts as retryable once.
- Item-level: a failed item is **not** retried inside the same run (avoids head-of-line
  blocking). It stays unmarked in the day-ledger and is naturally re-attempted by the next
  hourly run — the schedule itself is the retry mechanism.
- Circuit breaker: N consecutive Metacritic failures → abort run early, record reason.
  Prevents burning an hour hammering a site that is blocking us.

---

## 14. Idempotency & crash-safety

This is the heart of the brief, so it is specified precisely.

**Two-phase claim/complete against `daily_processed_game`:**

1. **Claim:** `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (day, game_slug) DO NOTHING RETURNING *`.
   Row returned → this worker owns the item. Nothing returned → someone else owns it, skip.
   The claim is atomic, so it doubles as the concurrency guard.
2. **Process** stages, persisting each stage's output as it completes.
3. **Complete:** update the row to `done` with stage detail.

**Recovery from every failure mode in the brief:**

| Scenario | Guarantee | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **App restart** | No duplicates, no loss | All state in Postgres; advisory lock auto-released on disconnect; next tick recomputes the plan from DB |
| **Worker crash** | Item retried, others unaffected | Item left `claimed`; a **stale-claim reaper** (claimed older than lease T) resets it to pending |
| **Job re-run** | Safe | Ledger claim rejects already-done slugs; `ON CONFLICT` upserts make game writes idempotent |
| **Parallel workers** | No double-processing | Atomic claim (row-level); only one wins each slug |
| **Partial processing** | Resumes, does not restart | Per-stage status + stage-level persistence; completed stages skipped on retry |

**Upsert key [ASSUMPTION]:** the Metacritic **slug** — stable, unique, present in every URL.
Titles are not unique (remakes/re-releases). See **OQ-4**.

The **stale-claim lease** is the subtle one: without it, a worker that dies mid-item leaves
that slug claimed forever and it silently never gets processed that day. The reaper closes
this hole.

---

## 15. Concurrency

Three independent levels, deliberately decoupled:

- **Run level:** at most one run globally — Postgres advisory lock. Protects against
  cron + force-run collision and against two app instances.
- **Item level:** worker pool (default 4) pulling claimed items. Safe because claiming is
  atomic.
- **Network level:** a **global token-bucket limiter shared by all workers**, ≤ 1 req/s to
  Metacritic. Critically, politeness is decoupled from pool size — raising concurrency never
  raises request rate against Metacritic. LLM/YouTube have separate limits.

Ordering: the brief implies sequential source order (A then B). The *plan* is ordered;
execution within a batch may be parallel — preserving required semantics without serialising
I/O.

---

## 16. Security

- Secrets via environment only; never committed. `.env.example` documents required keys.
- **Force-run endpoint must be protected** — it is an unauthenticated compute/cost trigger on
  a public URL. Recommend a shared-secret header or basic auth on write endpoints. **OQ-8**.
- Rate-limit write endpoints; strict input validation (zod) on all query params.
- SQL injection: parameterised queries only.
- XSS: scraped and LLM text is untrusted → escape on render; never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  Sanitise/allowlist embedded video URLs (known YouTube/Metacritic hosts only).
- SSRF: only fetch allowlisted hosts.
- No PII stored; user reviews are public content. Respect robots.txt and identify the bot
  honestly in the UA.

---

## 17. Performance

- Batch: 20 games × ~3 requests ≈ 60 requests at 1 req/s ≈ 1–2 min network-bound, plus LLM
  time (parallel, capped) → comfortably inside 10 min.
- Conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified) on re-crawled pages saves bandwidth and time.
- UI: server-side pagination, indexed sorts, trigram index for search, aggregates
  denormalised onto `game` to avoid per-row joins in the list view.
- Images: hotlink Metacritic CDN with lazy loading (**OQ-10** covers the alternative).
- Similarity computed on write, cached in `similar_game` — never computed per page view.

---

## 18. Cost

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| LLM summaries | 2 calls/game; cheap model; fingerprint gate makes re-crawls ~free → **low single-digit $** |
| YouTube API | Free tier; ~100 searches/day ceiling is the real constraint |
| Transcripts | Free if captions used; **paid ASR is the cost risk** (**OQ-5**) |
| Hosting | Small VPS / free-tier PaaS + managed Postgres ≈ **$0–7/mo** |
| **Total** | **≈ $5–10 for the evaluation period** |

Main cost lever is the fingerprint gate; second is ASR avoidance.

---

## CORE: Game processing logic (the central requirement)

### Day plan

`processing_day` holds, per calendar day: `phase`, `browse_page`, `new_releases_done`.

```
resolveBatch(day, N=20):
  ensure processing_day row for `day` (INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)

  if phase == 'new_releases':
      candidates = first 20 slugs from /game/   (New Releases)
      claimed    = claim(candidates)            -- skips already-done-today
      if claimed < N: top up from browse pages (advance cursor)
      when the New Releases set is fully processed today -> phase = 'browse'

  if phase == 'browse':
      loop:
        page        = browse_page
        candidates  = slugs from /browse/.../new/?page=page
        claimed    += claim(candidates)
        browse_page = page + 1                  -- persisted immediately
        until claimed == N or page limit hit
```

Because the batch derives from **DB state**, not run counters, it is automatically correct
after restarts, missed ticks, and manual runs.

### Daily reset

New calendar day → no `processing_day` row → created with `phase='new_releases'`,
`browse_page=1`. The cycle restarts naturally. **[ASSUMPTION]** the boundary is a fixed
configured timezone (not server-local) so behaviour is deterministic — **OQ-1**.

### VERIFIED RISK — the "next page" cursor is not stable

Live probing found that **page 1 and page 2 of the browse listing share 17 of 33 links**

releases* — page 1 was full of `Sep 7, 2026` and even `Sep 8, 2026` entries. New games are

a single page read.

### LLM summarization
See §10. Structured output, input sampled across the score spectrum, fingerprint-gated,
grounded prompt, JSONL-logged.

overlap + developer/publisher match + title trigram, weighted. Deterministic, zero marginal

|---|---|
| **0 — skeleton** | Repo, Docker Compose, migrations, health checks, CI |
| **1 — mandatory core** | Fetcher, parsers, day plan + ledger, upserts, hourly cron |
| **2 — mandatory UI** | List, detail, filter, search, sort |
| **3 — AI** | Review summaries (critic + user), JSONL logging |

| **6 — optional 1** | YouTube *(most expensive, riskiest — behind a flag)* |

Phase 6 because it is lower-risk, lower-cost, and far more visible to an evaluator per hour
invested.

# Open Questions — Metacritic Games Service

**Status:** awaiting decisions from Product/Tech Lead
**Date:** 2026-09-07

Every ambiguity found during discovery is listed here rather than silently resolved in code.
Each has options and a recommendation. **Blocking** items change the data model or core loop
and should be answered before Phase 1; the rest have safe defaults and can be deferred.

**Fast path:** if you agree with every recommendation, reply *"all recommended"* and I will
proceed on that basis. Items marked ⚠️ are the ones I would most like you to actually read.

---

## Priority summary

| ID | Topic | Blocking? | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-1 | Day boundary timezone | **Yes** | UTC, configurable |
| OQ-2 | Tech stack | **Yes** | Next.js + Node/TS + Postgres, modular monolith |
| OQ-3 ⚠️ | Developer vs publisher | **Yes** | Store both; show developer, fall back to publisher |
| OQ-4 | Game identity key | **Yes** | Metacritic slug |
| OQ-5 ⚠️ | YouTube transcript source | No (Phase 6) | Captions, graceful degrade, no paid ASR |
| OQ-6 | LLM provider/model | No | Cheap small model (Haiku-class) |
| OQ-7 | Realtime transport | No | SSE |
| OQ-8 ⚠️ | Force-run auth | No | Shared-secret header |
| OQ-9 | Cold-start seeding | No | Seed on first boot |
| OQ-10 | Image handling | No | Hotlink CDN |
| OQ-11 | Review volume cap | No | First page, ~30–50 each |
| OQ-12 | Similarity method | No | Content-based v1 |
| OQ-13 ⚠️ | "20 games" semantics | **Yes** | 20 claimed per run |
| OQ-14 | Re-crawl policy | No | Only if not yet processed today |
| OQ-15 | Hosting target | No | Single VPS + Docker Compose |
| OQ-16 | AI transcript scope | No | All LLM calls, redacted |
| OQ-17 | Historical backfill | No | No — forward-only |
| OQ-18 | Platform score source | No | Per-platform pages if cheap, else overall |

---

## OQ-1 — Which timezone defines "a day"? **[BLOCKING]**

"Each new day we start over" needs a concrete boundary.

- **A. UTC** — deterministic, no DST bugs.
- **B. Server local time** — surprising, changes if the host moves.
- **C. US/Pacific (Metacritic's own editorial day)** — best aligns our "new releases day"
  with theirs.
- **D. Configurable, default UTC.**

**Recommendation: D (default UTC).** One env var, deterministic, testable, and lets you
switch to Pacific later without a code change. DST bugs in day-boundary logic are a classic
source of "why did it run twice" incidents.

---

## OQ-2 — Technology stack **[BLOCKING]**

- **A. Node.js + TypeScript, Next.js (UI + API), Postgres, modular monolith.**
- **B. Node backend (Fastify) + separate React SPA.**
- **C. Python (FastAPI + BeautifulSoup) + separate frontend.**
- **D. Node + BullMQ/Redis for the queue.**

**Recommendation: A.** One language, one deployable, SSR for fast first paint, trivially
dockerised — which directly serves the "must be a live, working link" deliverable. Redis (D)
adds a moving part the workload does not justify; Postgres advisory locks cover the same
ground. Python (C) is a fine scraping stack but splits the codebase in two for no gain here.

*If you prefer Python or a queue-based design, say so now — it changes Phase 0 and 1.*

---

## OQ-3 ⚠️ — "Разработчик": developer or publisher? **[BLOCKING]**

The brief asks for **developer**. JSON-LD reliably provides **publisher** — for
`halloween-the-game` it returned *Gun Interactive* and *IllFonic*, which are publisher and
developer respectively, in one undifferentiated list **[VERIFIED]**. Metacritic's own detail
page shows both, but in less stable markup than JSON-LD.

- **A. Store both fields; parse developer from the page, publisher from JSON-LD; display
  developer and fall back to publisher when absent.**
- **B. Store only JSON-LD publisher and label it "Developer"** — simplest, but factually
  wrong on the page, which a reviewer may well notice.
- **C. Store only developer via CSS selectors** — accurate but fragile, and null whenever the
  selector breaks.

**Recommendation: A.** Cheap (one extra column), factually correct, and degrades sensibly.
Fully satisfies the requirement while surviving markup changes.

---

## OQ-4 — Primary identity key for a game **[BLOCKING]**

- **A. Metacritic slug** (e.g. `halloween-the-game`) — unique, stable, in every URL.
- **B. Title + release year.**
- **C. Title + platform.**

**Recommendation: A.** Titles are not unique (remakes, re-releases, regional variants) and
C would fragment one game into several rows, breaking the multi-platform requirement (FR-6).
Slug is what Metacritic itself uses as the identifier.

---

## OQ-5 ⚠️ — YouTube transcript source (optional part 1)

This is the **single riskiest item in the whole brief**. "Перевести рассказ блогера в текст"
implies real speech-to-text, but reliable transcript access is genuinely hard:

- **A. Official captions via YouTube Data API** — legitimate, free; **but many gaming videos
  have none**, and auto-captions are not exposed via the official API.
- **B. Third-party caption scraper (`youtube-transcript` etc.)** — usually works, gets
  auto-captions, but unofficial, fragile, ToS-grey.
- **C. Download audio + ASR (Whisper)** — always works, genuinely fulfils the requirement,
  but costs money/CPU, is slow (minutes per video), and downloading YouTube audio is against
  YouTube ToS.
- **D. Hybrid: try A, then B, else fall back to a conclusion from title/description/metadata,
  clearly labelled as not transcript-based.**

**Recommendation: D.** It attempts the real thing, degrades honestly rather than failing, and
avoids both the cost and the ToS exposure of C. The UI must state which source was used so we
never imply we transcribed audio when we did not.

**Decision needed:** is a labelled metadata-based fallback acceptable, or do you want true ASR
(accepting cost, latency, and ToS risk)?

---

## OQ-6 — LLM provider and model

- **A. Cheap small model (Haiku-class) for all three jobs.**
- **B. Mid-tier model for summaries.**
- **C. Local model (Ollama).**

**Recommendation: A.** These are summarisation-of-supplied-text tasks, not reasoning tasks;
a small model is sufficient and keeps total cost in single-digit dollars. C removes API cost
but needs hardware the demo host will not have.

---

## OQ-7 — Realtime transport (optional part 2)

- **A. SSE** — one-way, auto-reconnect, proxy-friendly, minimal code.
- **B. WebSockets** — bidirectional, more infrastructure.
- **C. Polling** — simplest, but not really "realtime".

**Recommendation: A.** The dashboard is strictly server→client; SSE covers it with the least
code and the fewest deployment surprises.

---

## OQ-8 ⚠️ — Should the force-run button be authenticated?

It is a publicly reachable endpoint that triggers scraping and paid LLM calls. Unprotected, a
crawler or curious visitor could spam it.

- **A. Shared-secret header / basic auth on write endpoints.**
- **B. Open, but rate-limited (1 run / 5 min) and idempotent via the run lock.**
- **C. Fully open.**

**Recommendation: A, with B's rate limit also applied.** The advisory lock already prevents
concurrent runs, so the risk is cost/nuisance rather than corruption — but leaving a paid
trigger open on a public URL is not something I would ship.

**Note:** if the evaluator must be able to press the button, the credential has to be in the
README or the button pre-authorised. Tell me which you prefer.

---

## OQ-9 — Cold-start seeding

A reviewer opening the link right after deploy would otherwise see an empty list (DR-5).

- **A. Run one ingestion immediately on first boot.**
- **B. Ship a seed SQL dump.**
- **C. Wait for the first cron tick** (up to 1 h of empty UI).

**Recommendation: A.** Honest (real scraped data), no fixture maintenance, and the service
looks alive within minutes. B is a fallback if Metacritic blocks us at review time.

---

## OQ-10 — Cover images: hotlink or self-host?

- **A. Hotlink Metacritic CDN** — zero storage, but breaks if they add referrer checks.
- **B. Download to local/object storage** — robust, adds storage and a pipeline stage.
- **C. Hotlink + lazy local caching.**

**Recommendation: A for MVP**, C if hotlinking proves unreliable. Storage costs and a new
failure mode are not justified for a demo.

---

## OQ-11 — How many reviews to fetch per game?

- **A. First page only (~10–15 critic, ~10–50 user).**
- **B. First N pages (2–3).**
- **C. All reviews** — dozens of requests for popular titles.

**Recommendation: A, with a configurable cap (~30–50 each).** Summary quality plateaus
quickly; C would blow the politeness budget and the batch-latency target for a marginal
quality gain.

---

## OQ-12 — Similar-games algorithm

- **A. Content-based:** genre + platform + developer/publisher + title trigram, weighted.
- **B. Embeddings** over description + reviews, vector search (pgvector).
- **C. Score/genre proximity only.**
- **D. LLM picks from candidates.**

**Recommendation: A for MVP, B as a documented upgrade.** A is deterministic, explainable,
free, needs no extra infrastructure, and is easy to demo. D adds cost and non-determinism per
game for little visible gain.

**Note:** with a small DB, early games have few good neighbours. I will enforce a minimum
similarity score and show fewer results rather than pad with poor matches.

---

## OQ-13 ⚠️ — Does "20 games" mean claimed or successfully completed? **[BLOCKING]**

If 5 of 20 fail, does the run process 20 or push on to 25 to reach 20 successes?

- **A. 20 *claimed* per run.** Failures roll into the next hourly run naturally.
- **B. Keep going until 20 *succeed*.** Unbounded run time and request count when the site
  misbehaves — exactly when we should be backing off.
- **C. 20 claimed, then one top-up round.**

**Recommendation: A.** Bounded, predictable, polite; the hourly schedule is the retry
mechanism (§13). B risks a run that never ends during an outage.

---

## OQ-14 — Should already-known games be re-crawled within the same day?

- **A. No** — once per game per day, matching "games not processed today".
- **B. Yes**, if data is older than N hours.
- **C. Separate low-frequency refresh job for stale popular games.**

**Recommendation: A** — it is the literal reading of the brief. C is a good post-MVP
addition if you want summaries to stay fresh for high-profile titles.

---

## OQ-15 — Hosting target for the live demo

- **A. Single small VPS + Docker Compose (app + Postgres).**
- **B. PaaS (Railway/Render/Fly) + managed Postgres.**
- **C. Serverless.**

**Recommendation: A or B — your call on ops preference.** A gives a stable outbound IP
(better for scraping) and predictable cost; B is faster to stand up and has a nicer URL. C is
a poor fit: long-running hourly workers and connection pooling fight the model.

**Decision needed:** do you already have a VPS/domain to use, or should I plan for a PaaS free
tier?

---

## OQ-16 — Scope of the required AI transcript logs

The brief asks for "всю переписку с нейросетью" as raw JSONL.

- **A. All production LLM calls** (summaries, conclusions) with prompt, response, model,
  tokens, timing.
- **B. A + the development-time assistant conversations.**
- **C. Runtime calls only, prompts redacted.**

**Recommendation: A**, committed to the repo, with API keys and PII redacted. If you also
want development conversations included (B), say so — it affects how I archive this session
and everything after it.

---

## OQ-17 — Historical backfill

- **A. No** — forward-only from first run, per the brief.
- **B. Backfill N pages on first run** for a fuller demo DB.

**Recommendation: A**, with the caveat that Phase 5's force-run button lets you press it a few
times before review to populate the DB naturally. That gets B's benefit without extra code.

---

## OQ-18 — Per-platform score extraction

FR-6 wants Metascore + Userscore **per platform**. JSON-LD gives one `aggregateRating` plus a
`gamePlatform` list **[VERIFIED]**; per-platform scores may require additional page visits.

- **A. Fetch each platform's page** — accurate, but multiplies request count per game.
- **B. Use the overall score for every listed platform** — cheap, slightly inaccurate.
- **C. Parse per-platform data from the detail page if present, else fall back to B.**

**Recommendation: C.** Correct when the data is there, cheap when it is not, and never
inflates the request budget. I will confirm the exact per-platform markup during Phase 1 and
report back if A turns out to be unavoidable.

---

## Questions I need answered before Phase 1

1. **OQ-3** — confirm developer/publisher handling.
2. **OQ-13** — confirm "20 claimed, not 20 completed".
3. **OQ-1 / OQ-2 / OQ-4** — confirm UTC, stack, slug key (or say "all recommended").
4. **OQ-5** — is a labelled non-ASR fallback acceptable for the YouTube part?
5. **OQ-15** — VPS or PaaS?

- **B. PaaS (Railway/Render/Fly) + managed Postgres.**
- **C. Serverless.**

**Recommendation: A or B — your call on ops preference.** A gives a stable outbound IP
(better for scraping) and predictable cost; B is faster to stand up and has a nicer URL. C is
a poor fit: long-running hourly workers and connection pooling fight the model.

**Decision needed:** do you already have a VPS/domain to use, or should I plan for a PaaS free
tier?

The brief asks for "всю переписку с нейросетью" as raw JSONL.

- **A. All production LLM calls** (summaries, conclusions) with prompt, response, model,

- **B. A + the development-time assistant conversations.**
- **C. Runtime calls only, prompts redacted.**

**Recommendation: A**, committed to the repo, with API keys and PII redacted. If you also
want development conversations included (B), say so — it affects how I archive this session
and everything after it.

**Recommendation: A**, with the caveat that Phase 5's force-run button lets you press it a few

content.text:
Both documents are written. No code, as instructed.

## 1. Key architectural risks

**R1 — The page cursor is not stable [VERIFIED, and the most important finding].** I probed the browse listing: **pages 1 and 2 share 17 of 33 links**. The list is sorted by release date descending *including future-dated entries* (page 1 held `Sep 7` and `Sep 8, 2026` games), so new rows are inserted at the top continuously and everything shifts rightward as you paginate. The brief's literal "process the next page each run" would therefore **re-read games already done and silently skip others**. Fix: the day-ledger is authoritative, the page number is only a hint, and the batch loop keeps advancing pages until it has claimed 20 genuinely-new slugs.

**R2 — Metacritic layout change or IP block.** The whole mandatory scope depends on one site with no API. Mitigated by JSON-LD-first parsing (a schema.org contract, far more stable than CSS classes), CSS fallback, golden-file fixture tests, ≤1 req/s, and abort-on-403 rather than retry-into-a-ban.

**R3 — YouTube transcripts (optional part 1).** The riskiest optional item. Official captions are often absent on gaming videos, auto-captions aren't exposed via the official API, scrapers are fragile and ToS-grey, and ASR costs money, time, and ToS exposure. Recommendation is graceful, clearly-labelled degradation — this needs your decision (OQ-5).

**R4 — Silent data loss from a dead worker.** Without a lease, a worker crashing mid-item leaves that slug claimed forever and it never gets processed that day — a bug that looks like nothing at all. Closed by a stale-claim reaper plus session-scoped advisory locks that Postgres releases automatically on disconnect.

**R5 — Empty UI at review time.** A reviewer opening a freshly deployed link sees nothing for up to an hour. Addressed by seeding on first boot (OQ-9).

**Good news that materially de-risks the project:** everything is server-rendered and reachable with plain curl — listings, detail pages, *and* both review pages (I pulled real critic review text and scores from `elden-ring/critic-reviews/` over raw HTTP). **No headless browser anywhere**, which removes the biggest cost and flakiness source. JSON-LD alone supplies 6 of the 7 required fields.

## 2. Open questions

18 total, in `docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`. Five are blocking:

- **OQ-3 ⚠️** — brief says *developer*, JSON-LD gives *publisher* (they're different; for `halloween-the-game` it returned Gun Interactive **and** IllFonic undifferentiated). Recommend storing both.
- **OQ-13 ⚠️** — does "20 games" mean 20 *claimed* or 20 *successfully completed*? Recommend claimed; "until 20 succeed" makes run time unbounded exactly when the site is misbehaving.
- **OQ-1** day-boundary TZ (→ UTC, configurable), **OQ-2** stack (→ Next.js + Node/TS + Postgres monolith), **OQ-4** identity key (→ slug).

Non-blocking but worth your eye: **OQ-5** YouTube transcripts, **OQ-8** whether the force-run button — a public, cost-incurring trigger — should be authenticated, **OQ-15** VPS vs PaaS, **OQ-16** whether the required AI transcripts should include our development conversations (that affects how I archive this session onward).

## 3. Recommended MVP scope

Phases 1–4 fully satisfy the mandatory brief: ingestion core (fetcher, parsers, day-plan + ledger, upserts, hourly cron) → UI (list, detail, filter, search, sort) → AI review summaries + JSONL logging → similar games.

Then **Phase 5 (monitoring + force run) before Phase 6 (YouTube)** — deliberately inverting the brief's optional-part numbering. Part 2 is cheaper, lower-risk, and far more visible per hour invested; part 1 carries the transcript risk and should go last, behind a feature flag, so it can be dropped without touching anything else.

Reply **"all recommended"** to accept every recommendation, or answer the five blocking questions and I'll start Phase 0.

Отлично. Принимаю результаты Discovery и предлагаемые рекомендации, но как Product/Tech Lead фиксирую следующие решения:

1. OQ-1:

* Day boundary: UTC.
* Timezone должна быть конфигурируемой через environment/config, но в demo используем UTC.

2. OQ-2:

* Используем модульный монолит.
* Frontend: Next.js + TypeScript.
* Backend/API: Node.js + TypeScript.
* Database: PostgreSQL.
* Не используем микросервисы на MVP.
* При этом доменные модули должны иметь чёткие границы и не зависеть напрямую от infrastructure/external providers.

3. OQ-3:

* В требованиях нужен developer.
* Если Metacritic позволяет достоверно определить developer отдельно от publisher — сохраняем оба поля.
* Никогда не подменяем developer publisher без явной маркировки.
* Если developer определить невозможно, сохраняем null/unknown и фиксируем это в ingestion logs.

4. OQ-4:

* Внутренний primary key: UUID.
* Внешний identity key Metacritic: canonical slug + source.
* Не полагаемся только на title.

5. OQ-5:

* YouTube transcripts реализуем как optional feature.
* Ошибка/отсутствие transcript никогда не должна ломать основной pipeline.
* Функциональность должна быть отключаемой feature flag.

6. OQ-8:

* Manual Force Run должен быть защищён authentication/authorization.
* Даже для demo не делаем публичный endpoint, который позволяет бесконтрольно запускать дорогие jobs.

7. OQ-13:

* "20 games" означает 20 уникальных игр, которые были успешно CLAIMED для обработки в рамках processing day.
* Claim должен быть идемпотентным.
* Повторный запуск не должен повторно claim одну и ту же игру в тот же processing day.
* Failed processing после claim должно иметь возможность retry/recovery через lease/reaper, но не создавать duplicate claim.

8. OQ-15:

* Deployment target: Docker Compose на VPS.
* Production-like setup, но без избыточной инфраструктуры.

9. OQ-16:

* Полная AI development history должна сохраняться.
* Raw logs не редактируются.
* Логи разных AI agents сохраняются отдельно.
* Дополнительно создаём merged JSONL audit trail.
* В merged log обязательно указываем agent, role, timestamp и message/event type.

10. YouTube:

* Реализовать после обязательной части и monitoring.
* Feature flag.
* Graceful degradation.
* Не допускать, чтобы отсутствие transcript блокировало обработку игры.

Дополнительные архитектурные требования:

* Не использовать микросервисы.
* Использовать domain/application/infrastructure separation внутри модульного монолита.
* External integrations должны быть скрыты за interfaces/adapters.
* Scraped content и YouTube transcripts считать untrusted input.
* Background jobs должны быть idempotent.
* Все внешние HTTP requests должны иметь timeout, retry policy и понятную обработку 403/429/5xx.
* Не использовать headless browser без доказанной необходимости.
* Все критичные assumptions фиксировать в документации.
* Не invent API contracts или selectors: сначала исследование, затем implementation.
* Каждое значимое архитектурное решение оформить ADR.

# ЗАКРЫТЫЕ ВОПРОСЫ

## ✅ OQ-1 — Граница суток

**РЕШЕНИЕ:** день определяется по **UTC**. Timezone обязана быть конфигурируемой через
environment/config (`PROCESSING_TIMEZONE`), в demo используется UTC.

**Следствия:** ключ `processing_day.day` вычисляется через конфигурируемую TZ, а не через
время сервера. Смена TZ не должна требовать изменения кода. См. **ADR-0002**.

---

## ✅ OQ-2 — Технологический стек

**РЕШЕНИЕ:**
- Модульный монолит; микросервисы на MVP не используются.
- Frontend: **Next.js + TypeScript**.
- Backend/API: **Node.js + TypeScript**.
- Database: **PostgreSQL**.
- Доменные модули обязаны иметь чёткие границы и **не зависеть напрямую от
  infrastructure/external providers**.

**Следствия:** внутри монолита обязательна раскладка domain / application / infrastructure.
Внешние интеграции скрыты за интерфейсами (портами). См. **ADR-0001**.

---

## ✅ OQ-3 — Developer vs Publisher

**РЕШЕНИЕ:**
- В требованиях нужен **developer**.
- Если Metacritic позволяет достоверно определить developer отдельно от publisher —
  сохраняем **оба** поля.
- **Никогда** не подменяем developer publisher'ом без явной маркировки.
- Если developer определить невозможно — сохраняем `null`/`unknown` и фиксируем это в
  ingestion logs.

### Результат дополнительного исследования (2026-09-07) — решение подтверждено фактами

Проведена проверка на 4 играх **[ПРОВЕРЕНО]**:

| Игра | developer (DOM) | publisher (JSON-LD) |
|---|---|---|
| `elden-ring` | From Software | Bandai Namco Games, **From Software** |
| `halloween-the-game` | IllFonic | Gun Interactive, **IllFonic** |
| `hot-wheels-infinite-rush` | Milestone S.r.l | Milestone S.r.l |
| `the-blood-of-dawnwalker` | **(пусто)** | Bandai Namco Games |

**Ключевые выводы:**

1. **Developer доступен отдельно** — в контейнере
   `data-testid="hero-summary-developer"` со ссылкой вида `/company/from-software/`.
   Присутствует в 4/4 проверенных страниц. Атрибут `data-testid` стабильнее CSS-классов.
2. **JSON-LD `publisher` смешивает издателя и разработчика в один список** — для Elden Ring
   он вернул и Bandai Namco, и From Software без различения ролей. Использовать его как
   developer было бы фактически неверно — политика «не подменять» подтверждена.
3. **Случай пустого developer реален, а не гипотетичен** — `the-blood-of-dawnwalker` не имеет
   developer в разметке. Ветка `null/unknown` + ingestion log обязательна к реализации.

**Правило извлечения:** developer — из `data-testid="hero-summary-developer"`; publisher — из
JSON-LD; при отсутствии developer → `null`, `developer_status = 'unknown'`, запись в
ingestion log. Подмена запрещена на уровне кода. См. **ADR-0003**.

---

## ✅ OQ-4 — Идентичность игры

**РЕШЕНИЕ:**
- Внутренний primary key: **UUID**.
- Внешний identity key Metacritic: **canonical slug + source**.
- Не полагаться только на title.

**Следствия:** `game.id UUID PK`; `UNIQUE (source, source_slug)` как natural key для upsert.
Поле `source` заранее закладывает возможность второго источника без миграции PK.
См. **ADR-0003**.

---

## ✅ OQ-5 / YouTube — Transcripts как optional feature

**РЕШЕНИЕ:**
- Реализуется **после** обязательной части и monitoring.
- Управляется **feature flag**.
- Ошибка или отсутствие transcript **никогда** не ломает основной pipeline.
- Graceful degradation обязательна.

**Следствия:** стадия YouTube полностью изолирована; её падение не влияет на статус игры.
При выключенном флаге код не выполняется и не требует API-ключей. См. **ADR-0005**.

---

## ✅ OQ-7 — Realtime transport

**РЕШЕНИЕ:** **SSE** (принята рекомендация Discovery). Поток данных односторонний
server→client, SSE автоматически переподключается и не требует отдельной инфраструктуры.

---

## ✅ OQ-8 — Authentication для Force Run

**РЕШЕНИЕ:** Manual Force Run **обязан** быть защищён authentication/authorization. Даже для
demo не допускается публичный endpoint, позволяющий бесконтрольно запускать дорогие jobs.

**Следствия:** все write-эндпоинты требуют аутентификации; дополнительно применяется
rate limit. Способ доступа для проверяющего описывается в README.

> **Уточнение (не блокирующее):** предлагаю статический токен в заголовке (`X-Admin-Token`),
> значение передаётся отдельно и указывается в README как demo-credential. Если хотите
> вместо этого basic auth или логин-форму — скажите, это меняет объём Фазы 5.

---

## ✅ OQ-13 — Семантика «20 игр»

**РЕШЕНИЕ:** «20 games» = **20 уникальных игр, успешно CLAIMED** в рамках processing day.
- Claim обязан быть **идемпотентным**.
- Повторный запуск **не должен** повторно claim одну и ту же игру в тот же processing day.
- Failed processing после claim обязан иметь retry/recovery через **lease/reaper**,
  **не создавая duplicate claim**.

**Следствия:** это ядро корректности сервиса. См. **ADR-0004**.

---

## ✅ OQ-15 — Deployment

**РЕШЕНИЕ:** **Docker Compose на VPS**, production-like setup без избыточной инфраструктуры.

**Следствия:** compose поднимает app + PostgreSQL (+ reverse proxy с TLS). Стабильный
исходящий IP — плюс для scraping. Никаких Kubernetes/очередей на MVP.

---

## ✅ OQ-16 — AI development history

**РЕШЕНИЕ:**
- Полная AI development history сохраняется.
- Raw logs **не редактируются**.
- Логи разных AI agents сохраняются **отдельно**.
- Дополнительно создаётся **merged JSONL audit trail**.
- В merged log обязательны: `agent`, `role`, `timestamp`, `message/event type`.

**Следствия:** структура `logs/ai/raw/<agent>/*.jsonl` + `logs/ai/merged/audit-trail.jsonl`.
Отдельно логируются runtime LLM-вызовы сервиса. См. **DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md**.

> ⚠️ **Важное следствие для безопасности.** Требование «raw logs не редактируются» вступает
> в конфликт со стандартной практикой redaction секретов. Практическое разрешение: секреты
> **никогда не попадают** в промпты и логи (запрет на уровне кода), поэтому редактировать
> постфактум нечего. Raw-логи остаются нетронутыми. Перед публикацией репозитория логи
> проверяются автоматическим сканером секретов — при срабатывании вопрос эскалируется вам,
> а не решается тихой правкой. См. **OQ-19**.

---

# ОСТАЮЩИЕСЯ ОТКРЫТЫЕ ВОПРОСЫ

Ниже — вопросы с безопасными значениями по умолчанию. Реализация может идти на
рекомендованных вариантах; ваше решение требуется только при несогласии.

## ⚠️ OQ-6 — LLM провайдер и модель

Зафиксирована дешёвая модель, но **провайдер не назван**.
- **A. Anthropic Claude (Haiku-класс)** — структурированный вывод, дешёвый.
- **B. OpenAI (mini-класс).**
- **C. Локальная модель** — VPS demo её не потянет.

**Рекомендация: A.** Требуется подтверждение, какой API-ключ будет доступен на VPS.
Провайдер скрыт за портом `LlmProvider`, поэтому замена — это один адаптер.

---

## ⚠️ OQ-9 — Cold-start seeding

**Рекомендация:** выполнять один прогон ingestion при первом старте, чтобы проверяющий
не увидел пустой список. Альтернатива — ждать первого тика cron (до 1 часа пустого UI).

---

## ⚠️ OQ-10 — Обложки: hotlink или自 хранение

**Рекомендация:** hotlink CDN Metacritic + lazy loading на MVP. Переход на локальное
хранение — при появлении referrer-проверок.

---

## ⚠️ OQ-11 — Объём отзывов на игру

**Рекомендация:** первая страница, cap 30–50 отзывов каждого типа. Качество summary выходит
на плато быстро, а полный обход ломает бюджет вежливости и целевую длительность батча.

---

## ⚠️ OQ-12 — Алгоритм похожих игр

**Рекомендация:** content-based v1 (жанры + платформы + developer/publisher + trigram по
названию, со взвешиванием). Детерминирован, бесплатен, объясним. Эмбеддинги — путь развития.

---

## ⚠️ OQ-14 — Повторный обход игры в тот же день

**Рекомендация:** не повторять — это буквальное прочтение ТЗ («игры, которые сегодня не
обрабатывал»). Отдельный низкочастотный refresh-job — кандидат на post-MVP.

---

## ⚠️ OQ-17 — Исторический backfill

**Рекомендация:** forward-only. Кнопка Force Run позволяет наполнить БД перед демонстрацией
без дополнительного кода.

---

## 🔬 OQ-18 — Per-platform Metascore/Userscore **[ТРЕБУЕТ ИССЛЕДОВАНИЯ]**

FR-6 требует Metascore + Userscore **по каждой платформе**. Подтверждено, что JSON-LD даёт
один общий `aggregateRating` и список `gamePlatform` **[ПРОВЕРЕНО]**. Способ получения
именно per-platform оценок **пока не подтверждён разметкой**.

Согласно вашему требованию «не invent selectors: сначала исследование» — этот вопрос
намеренно оставлен открытым и вынесен отдельной задачей в начало Фазы 1.

Варианты после исследования:
- **A.** Per-platform данные есть на странице игры → парсим оттуда (дёшево).
- **B.** Требуются отдельные страницы платформ → +N запросов на игру (дорого, бьёт по
  бюджету вежливости).
- **C.** Данных нет → сохраняем общий score и явно маркируем платформы как «оценка общая».

**Рекомендация:** C как гарантированный fallback, A как целевой вариант. B принимать только
если A недоступен, и с пересчётом бюджета запросов. Результат исследования → ADR.

---

## 🆕 OQ-19 — Порядок действий при обнаружении секрета в raw AI logs

Возник из решения OQ-16 («raw logs не редактируются»).

- **A. Секреты не попадают в логи by design; перед публикацией — автоматический скан;
  при срабатывании эскалация вам.**
- **B. Редактировать найденное** — нарушает «не редактируем».
- **C. Не проверять** — риск утечки ключа в публичном репозитории.

**Рекомендация: A.** Сохраняет требование неизменности raw-логов и при этом не допускает
публикации секрета молча.

---

## 🆕 OQ-20 — Глубина «History» для AI logs

Требуется ли включать в merged audit trail **только** сессии по данному проекту, или все
взаимодействия с AI-агентами независимо от темы?

- **A. Только сессии данного проекта** — релевантно, компактно.
- **B. Всё подряд** — рискует включить постороннее и приватное.

**Рекомендация: A.**

---

## Вопросы, требующие вашего ответа перед Фазой 1

1. **OQ-6** — какой LLM-провайдер/ключ будет доступен на VPS?
2. **OQ-8 (уточнение)** — статический admin-токен достаточен, или нужен basic auth / форма?
3. **OQ-19 / OQ-20** — подтвердить политику по секретам и охвату логов.

Остальные открытые вопросы имеют безопасные defaults и не блокируют старт.
